motivation.observed_failure: the nearest-surface XHand residual passed A by +1/-0 but became +3/-3 on D; moving closer rescued Clock/Pan/Thumbtack yet destroyed Can/Palette/SoapBottle
motivation.diagnosis: distance to any surface is unsigned and has no semantic side information, so a finger can approach a nearby but mechanically wrong object face
motivation.new_hypothesis: the local object patch actually approached by the same Shadow expert finger carries more useful contact-side information than the globally nearest target-hand surface point

method.activation_gate: unchanged: Shadow fingertip within 20 mm and target fingertip nearest-surface gap more than 3 mm larger
method.expert_region: 32 object vertices nearest to the corresponding Shadow fingertip at the expert grasp frame
method.objective: numerically minimize target fingertip distance to that semantic local region using only the activated finger's joints
method.temporal_application: ramp from close to grasp and preserve a constant residual afterward, leaving wrist and original lift dynamics unchanged
method.joint_limits: effective residual is bounded against all 70 frames; no post-hoc clipping is allowed

why_32_neighbors: a single mesh vertex is sensitive to tessellation, while 32 vertices define a small local patch already used by the earlier contact-region prototype; it preserves the expert side without requiring a new region-size sweep
difference_from_prior_methods: unlike adaptive_finger_gap_v1 it does not optimize distance to the entire object
unlike the rejected full XHand contact refinement it does not jointly optimize the wrist or all fingers
it does not freeze the lift phase and does not query physics success while generating a candidate
selection_rule: within each hand require success_count above the current A baseline and positive paired net gain; at most one cap may enter E; ties choose 0.05 rad; E must again have positive net gain before replacing the current method
